sentences.show: For three centuries, the sailor's sword was the cutlass. In 1936, the Royal Navy retired it.
From then on, cutlasses were for ceremony, not for fighting.
Short enough to swing below decks, strong enough to cut through rope.
Boys in the navy drilled with it. Pirates swore by it.
It was the weapon of the boarding party.
But the story didn't quite end there.
In 1940, the German ship Altmark hid in a Norwegian fjord, with 299 British prisoners.
The destroyer Cossack went in, boarded her, and set them free.
Legend says it was the last time British sailors boarded with cutlasses.
Many historians doubt it. They point to China, in 1900.
Today, chief petty officers still carry one, when they escort the flag.
Also on this day: a New York bank run set off the Panic of nineteen oh-seven, and India sent a probe to the Moon.
